item.title: 0.6.3-beta.1
item.description:
# Agent HUD 0.6.3-beta.1
## Compatibility
**Requires Agent HUD for iPhone 1.7.2 or later** for iPhone and Apple Watch sync. Update the iPhone app before updating the Mac. Older iPhone versions cannot read this release's data.
[Get the iPhone app](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6812113619).
If the required iPhone version is not yet on the App Store, cross-device features require the corresponding TestFlight version.
Requires an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 14 or later.
## Changes
### New
- Speaks nine languages: English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, French, German, Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese. Pick one in Settings → General → Language, or let it follow the system. - Adds "Take me around" to the card that tells what an update adds. It starts the getting-started tour beside the HUD, and the card counts as read. - Reads Qoder, QoderWork, TRAE, WorkBuddy, CodeBuddy, ZCode and MiniMax Code accounts from each app's own sign-in. Each region is its own account: Qoder CN, TRAE CN and CodeBuddy CN show apart from the international ones. - Lets agents start DeepSeek Harness sessions, through Agent HUD's plugin in a running Harness. With none running, the Harness desktop app opens. - Lets an agent that reads the answer itself leave out the reply line (#75). With `reply_hint: false` on `send_message` or `start_session`, the message ends by asking the recipient to answer in its turn, instead of sending a message back. - Opens the windows a sign-in page asks for beside the sign-in window, and presents the system's own browser to the site, so sign-ins that open a second window or check the browser go through.
### Fixes
- Delivers agent messages to Antigravity on Windows (#77). Finding Antigravity's server took over 6 seconds on some computers, longer than a message may wait, so every message was refused. It now takes milliseconds. - Stops marking CodeBuddy, Qoder CN and QoderWork as "Requests only" on the Remote page; their conversations sync to the phone too.

# Agent HUD 0.6.8
## Compatibility
**Requires Agent HUD for iPhone 1.7.2 or later** for iPhone and Apple Watch sync. Update the iPhone app before updating the Mac. Older iPhone versions cannot read this release's data.
[Get the iPhone app](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6812113619).
Requires an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 14 or later.
## Changes
### New
- **Auto-hide for Simple docks.** Turn on Auto-hide in Settings → Display → HUD, off by default, and an idle Simple dock steps back against its edge and lets clicks through to the app beneath. At the edge chooses what stays there: the logos, a bar, or nothing. The bar has its own length, thickness and colour, and turns yellow or red as a usage limit nears. Pointing at the edge, a request, a message or a copy brings the dock back. The Notch HUD never hides (#119, thanks @QFAN04; #127, thanks @CSTGYYDS1). - **Quota reading per agent.** In Settings → Agents, where an agent's accounts are listed, Quota reading says how far Agent HUD goes to read its quota. Everything, the default, reads as before. Own app only leaves out sign-ins other apps keep, such as the Claude desktop app's for Claude and Pi's ChatGPT sign-in for Codex. Off shows no quota; sessions and tokens are still counted from the agent's logs. Claude and Codex offer all three, the other agents with a quota reader Off and Everything. Grok Bot uses Cursor's sign-in only while Cursor's Quota reading is Everything (#133, thanks @remio666). - **Shortest window first**, a switch per screen in Settings → Display → HUD where a Simple HUD writes numbers: the number beside each logo is its shortest window's, such as the 5-hour one, rather than the most used. The rim glow, the number's colour and the menu bar still follow the most used window (#122, thanks @Ultroncn, from @hbin-max's idea in #66). - Dropping a Simple dock at the notch turns it into the Notch HUD, as dragging the notch away already turns it into a Simple dock (macOS). - New Pi and OpenCode sessions can be started from the iPhone and from the inspector, on a computer where their command line is installed. Each starts in the client's own model, and Pi or OpenCode lists and resumes it like any other. Agents' `start_session` still starts only Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and DeepSeek Harness sessions. - The inspector also sends to Antigravity, and to a Pi or OpenCode session that is open in its client. It lists only the agents turned on in Agent HUD, and Claude Code and DeepSeek Harness only while their Send messages switch is on. Words you send fly as a paper plane from the bubble to the session. - Agents can steer a message into a DeepSeek Harness session's turn in progress when you ask them to, as with Codex (#125, thanks @xunhe730). Restart DeepSeek Harness once so it loads the plugin that takes a steer; `list_sessions` says which sessions can. - Statistics → Subscriptions and balances shows a signed-in Antigravity account's Google AI plan (Plus, Pro, Ultra 5x or Ultra 20x) at its monthly price, instead of "No signed-in plan for this agent" (#126, thanks @CSTGYYDS1).
### Fixes
- On the iPhone, a Claude, Codex, Cursor or Grok CLI account signed in on two computers shows one quota card instead of two. Both computers need this version. A Codex sign-in without an email still shows once per computer (#131, thanks @Niko-Echo). - `start_session` into Antigravity Desktop starts the conversation inside the project that holds its folder, so Antigravity's sidebar lists it there. A folder that two projects share still gets a conversation of its own (#123, thanks @cdk1025 for the patch). - The HUD stays inside the screen's work area, so a HUD docked to the bottom sits above the taskbar and stays visible after you click the taskbar (#121, Windows, thanks @yakura-OWO). - `send_message` and `start_session` to Codex use the `codex` the Codex app carries before a standalone one from npm, WinGet or PATH, and look again at every launch, so an old standalone `codex` no longer refuses messages with `unknown variant thread/queue/add`. The Mac has done this since 0.6.7 (#94, Windows, thanks @quwen1112-debug). - Agent HUD finds Claude Code, Codex and the other command lines installed through npm, pnpm, Scoop, Volta, nvm, fnm or WinGet, including behind `.cmd` shims, and starts them through the program or Node script the shim names, so a prompt with line breaks still goes through (#120, Windows, thanks @QFAN04). - Going back to an Antigravity, Codex or DeepSeek Harness session brings its window to the front, and wakes Antigravity from the tray. An Antigravity conversation opens when Antigravity has a single window; otherwise its log is shown. DeepSeek Harness opens through its registered `dsh://` link, which names the session for when Harness reads it; today's Harness brings its window forward (#130 and #132, Windows, thanks @zqy5618 and @FGBKILO-AGS). - Going back to a session opens it at once, instead of waiting while Agent HUD reads sessions (#130, thanks @zqy5618). - When a DeepSeek Harness turn ends, the HUD shows the end of its reply, as it does for other agents, and a session you just wrote in moves up the list before Harness answers (#130, thanks @zqy5618). - Approve automatically now reaches Claude Code. Claude Code asked on its own, because its hook missed an answer that came back at once (macOS). - A HUD on the right or bottom edge no longer flashes across the screen or vanishes for a moment when it is picked up, dropped, opened or closed (macOS). - The iPhone's local network reading no longer fails as a whole, with "The Mac's update did not match this connection", over one record the phone finds wrong: Agent HUD leaves that record out and sends the rest. Re-pairing did not help. - Quotas and balances are read a little more often: every 2 minutes while an agent works and every 4 otherwise, down from 2½ and 5. DeepSeek's balance is also read soon after a Claude Code, Codex or Pi turn that spends it through a DeepSeek key, not only after DeepSeek Harness's own turns. - The Chrome Web Store button in Settings opens the listing in Chrome or another Chromium browser that can add the extension, not in Safari. The browser extension's row in Settings turns on as soon as the extension is added, without leaving the page (macOS). - Agent HUD no longer stops at launch with "The private IPC directory ACL could not be set" on a PC whose security software blocks that change: a folder that is already private is left alone, and the message names the Windows error when one can't be made private (Windows). - Settings and the HUD draw with `LANG=C.UTF-8` or `POSIX`. Every window stayed blank and the HUD never appeared (Linux). - The `.deb` installs the tray's appindicator (`libayatana-appindicator3-1`). 0.6.7's package left it out, and Agent HUD stopped at launch on a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux).
